asi.pitfalls_found: four separate numeric landmines, each of which destroyed parity: (1) the Taylor coefficients for the natural-log Cody-Waite remainder must be 1/k! - the 2^r series coefficients are ln2^k/k!, and mixing them is off by e^r/2^r; (2) three Newton reciprocal steps leaves 2e-4 relative error, which this model turns into SNDR 10 dB - four steps are needed; (3) exp(2x)-1 near x=0 cancels away all significant digits (rel 3e-4 on tanh) - use the odd Taylor series for |x|<0.25; (4) 1/(1+exp(-x)) overflows to inf where the true sigmoid is ~1e-39 - branch to exp(x) for x<-87. asi.learned: Moving ~36 ms of host work onto the GPU loader makes N=4 worse: at N=4 the GPU is the bottleneck and extra per-load work is paid four times, while the host has spare cores. Do not trade host work for GPU work for the N=4 metric.
asi.crash_root_cause: The official run produced one wrong stream (L=57600, SNDR -1.98 dB) on the cold first process after a build. Not reproducible in 24 warm N=4 runs (12 with the patch, 12 without). Root cause in kept code since e072b0b: weights_upload() guards with a non-atomic '++g_wref > 1'; a stream arriving mid-upload returns immediately and runs inference while weight_ctab() hands out cudaMalloc'd device pointers whose cudaMemcpy has not happened yet, so it computes with garbage weights. weights_release() has the same race (possible double free). A cold run makes the upload slower and widens the window.
asi.next_action_hint: Fix the upload/release race with a mutex (correctness, not optional): streams arriving mid-upload must wait for it to finish. Then re-measure.

description: Fix two startup data races (weights_upload/release refcount+upload under a mutex; consumer-table build under a mutex): matched official N=4 2756/2670/2795/2785 vs 3156/3104/3130 (-12%) - the gain is all in startup (wall minus slowest stream 1.13 -> 0.72 s), inference unchanged (slowest stream +2-4%, N=1 flat); bit-exact

asi.what: weights_upload() guarded the shared GPU weight upload with a non-atomic '++g_wref > 1'; weights_release() decremented with '--g_wref'; pt_v21_open built the global consumer tables (g_n_cons/g_cons_node) behind an unlocked 'if (!g_cons_built)'. All three are data races between concurrently opened contexts. Now each is under a pthread mutex; late streams wait for the upload to finish.
asi.evidence: Matched measure.sh, alternating: nolock n4 3156/3104/3130 (slowest 2001/1955/2064, n1 767/766/769); lock n4 2756/2670/2795 plus run_experiment 2785 (slowest 2027/2037/2132/1919, n1 779/1474 cold/771/769). Bit-identical on 5 cases.
asi.honest_framing: The -12% is startup, not inference: wall minus slowest stream falls from ~1.13 s to ~0.72 s. Without the lock the three late streams start inference during stream 0's upload, pull weights through per-call fallback cudaMalloc+copy and contend with that upload, delaying stream 0. A warm server pays the upload once, so this matters for a cold burst of concurrent requests, not for steady-state per-request latency.
asi.correction_to_55: #55 attributed its one wrong stream to the upload race. That is NOT confirmed: stress tests that widened the malloc->memcpy window (2 ms and 30 ms per record) never produced a wrong stream with or without the lock, and a timeline showed late streams running their whole inference during the upload with correct output. The bad stream (1 in ~100+ N=4 runs, in a build with the discarded lrelu_fwd patch) is unexplained; 0 failures in 30 cold-ish runs of kept code (15 at a2cce50+locks, 15 at 0f77b25).
asi.next_action_hint: Inference per stream at N=4 ~2.0 s (GPU-bound, ~4 x 0.38 s GPU plus governor ramp). Remaining startup ~0.72 s: container open + fp32 conversion (serialized, ~85 MB) + upload; converting fp16 records on the GPU, or uploading directly from the mmap without the fp32 host copy, would shrink it, but that is startup-only. Ask the operator before optimizing startup further.
